citation.title: Electron cyclotron emission diagnostics on KSTAR tokamak
citation.authors: S. H. Jeong; K. D. Lee; Y. Kogi; K. Kawahata; Y. Nagayama; A. Mase; M. Kwon

topic: KSTAR ECE heterodyne radiometer hardware, calibration, and early electron temperature measurements from the second campaign.
own_question: Describe a 48-channel 110–162 GHz ECE system and report its initial operation.
actual_method_and_evidence: The paper describes the instrument and a hot/cold chopper calibration that averaged more than ten megasamples per channel. It reports electron temperature profiles at the high-field side from a 2 T campaign and qualitative sawtooth observations with spectra. Harmonic overlap is described as suspected for channels 22–40. There is no CES, ion temperature, nowcasting, BES/ECEI fusion, or prediction.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: ECE heterodyne radiometry offers fast electron-temperature measurements on KSTAR, assuming optically thick plasma.
claim_checks.qualification: Applies to electron Te from the 2010-era system, not to ECEI or to the KSTAR 2022 hardware. It says nothing about impurity Ti.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: ECE was digitized at a 50 kHz sampling rate during calibration. There is no relation to the 10 ms grid or to CES report timing.
validation_if_relevant: None; the paper reports qualitative observations only.
forbidden_inferences: ECE signals provide carbon-impurity CES temperature
the 2010 calibration applies to KSTAR 2022 ECEI voltages
the harmonic overlap mechanism was confirmed
prior KSTAR work performed causal nowcasting
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Optional background citation for KSTAR electron-cyclotron diagnostics only. Our inputs are ECEI voltage snapshots, not calibrated ECE Te, so this paper is weakly relevant.
source_scope_note: All extracted page texts supplied; figure/equation visual validation remains separate
